subject: QBR capacity synthesis + decision asks (GPU spend, util, batching/caching)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: QBR capacity synthesis + decision asks (GPU spend, util, batching/caching)

Hi team,

Ahead of the QBR (week of 6/19) I pulled together a short synthesis and a few explicit asks so leadership can sign off quickly. Attached: QBR_capacity_onepager.pdf + capacity_scenarios.csv. Quick summary below — please review and flag anything you think needs to move to the exec slide deck.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Demand baseline: 21M tokens/day served in hosted API (typical seq len ~128).
- Growth assumption for QBR: +45% demand by EOY if growth acceleration hits.
- Baseline fleet (mixed A100/V100-equivalent): 64 GPUs reserved today, average util = 58%, 95th p99 latency budget tight for interactive tiers.
- Unit economics: blended cost per GPU-hour (cloud + infra overhead) = $4.10; per-1000-token cost at baseline = $0.022.

Decision asks (for QBR slides):
1) Reserve uplift: Approve a committed pool increase to 96 GPUs (50% uplift) for Q3 with monthly billing; we need a yes/no so Procurement can lock SKUs. Impact: add ~$15k/month committed spend but reduces on-demand tail by ~30% and reduces per-token cost to ~$0.017 under projected util.
2) Utilization target: Set 75% target as our operational KPI for reserved pools (was 70%). If we take 75% we must schedule two batching experiments and promote KV prefix caching for top 40% of routes.
3) Batching/caching tradeoffs: We should accept a modest tail latency increase (p99 +40–80ms) on non-SLA tiers in exchange for 12–18% token-cost savings. Need sign-off on a canary schedule.
4) Contention fallback: Approve an automatic fallback to a smaller-but-faster model variant for non-critical routes when GPU queue > 85% for > 2 minutes.

Where I need you:
- Lauren: can you own the slide that compares committed vs on-demand economics (include blended per-token cost, runway impact)?
- Karthik: can you validate the batching experiments (3 configs) and updated latency numbers in the attached CSV? I noted three candidate configs in capacity_scenarios.csv.
- Marissa: please verify the utilization numbers in slot_utilization_q1-q2.csv and add Q2 trends on the slide.

Meeting ask: I propose a 35-minute dry run with the exec slide deck on 6/17 09:00–09:35 PT. If that works, I will loop in Finance and Procurement.

Thanks — Mark

--
Markus Klein
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 9, 2028 at 08:14 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Executive summary (TL;DR):
> - Demand baseline: 21M tokens/day served in hosted API
> - Decision asks: Reserve uplift to 96 GPUs, Util target 75%, batching/caching canary

Thanks Markus — this is crisp and exactly the level the execs want.

Notes and commitments:
- I will take the committed vs on-demand slide. I'll model three finance scenarios: conservative (flat growth), base (+25%), and stretch (+45%). Please confirm which scenario should be the recommended default (I assume base).
- I'll show the monthly P&L delta and a 6-month runway impact for the committed uplift. If Procurement needs line-item language for the contract, I can draft it with Legal.
- Dry run: 6/17 09:00 works for me; I'm blocking time.

Quick question for Karthik/Marissa: can we include an experiment row that isolates KV-prefix caching only (no batching) so execs can see the marginal benefit of caching vs batching? That will help with risk framing.

Lauren
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity synthesis + decision asks (GPU spend, util, batching/caching)

Markus / Lauren — attaching slot_utilization_q1-q2.csv with raw samples. Key things I validated:

- Measured utilization (fleet-weighted): Q1 = 56.8%, Q2 (to-date) = 62.4%. Trendline supports pushing target to 75% but we need rollout controls.
- Batching experiments (from the test cluster):
   * Batch A (aggressive): mean latency -14ms, p95 +6ms, p99 +72ms, cost reduction ~18%
   * Batch B (balanced): mean latency -8ms, p95 +2ms, p99 +38ms, cost reduction ~12%
   * Cache-only: mean latency -6ms, p95 -2ms, p99 +12ms, cost reduction ~9%
- Observability: need an alert when prefix cache hit rate < 28% on a route and when GPU queue > 80% for 3 continuous minutes.

Action items I will take before the dry run:
1) Add a dedicated "Cache-only" experiment row to capacity_scenarios.csv (done).
2) Produce a small chart showing tradeoffs (cost delta vs p99 delta) for the three experiments and put it on the appendix slide.
3) Pull a 30-day tail-latency histogram to validate impact on interactive tiers.

I also pinged Procurement (Gavin) separately to get a quick feasibility read on SKUs and committed pricing. He replied that committed capacity buy is doable but Finance will need a 6–12 month commit window for best discounts.

- Marissa
Sr. Manager, Capacity & Performance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: slot_utilization_q1-q2.csv (csv), experiment_latency_hist.png (png)

Markus / Marissa / Lauren — thanks for the heads up. Quick procurement note from my side: 

- Committed pool upgrade to 96 GPUs is feasible with our cloud partner. They offer a 22–28% discount on committed instances vs on-demand depending on commit duration.
- Recommendation: 9–12 month commit to secure the mid-point discount (25%). 3-month ramp allowed, with option to scale up/down at quarter boundaries (with 60-day notice).
- I will need the exact SKU mix (A100 vs T4-equivalent split), expected sustained util by SKU, and a forecasted monthly GPU-hour profile for the 6-month window to lock the contract.

If you can get me that by Thursday 6/14 EOD I can finish term sheets for Finance/Legal to review. I'll attach a short contract_reserve_summary_v2.pdf with standard language.

— Gavin
CloudProcure — Strategic Accounts
